No such test exists: grep for 'bead fetched by ID' across all *_test.go returns ZERO hits — the bypass line at next.go (runEmitOnly positional branch) can be deleted and the whole tree stays green, violating the repo's red-on-revert discipline for an explicitly AC-pinned surface.

Today the bypass line has zero test coverage — deleting it goes green.

findings.title: AC-10's positional --emit-only exception leg is unpinned (bypass line untested)
findings.detail: Spec AC-10: 'Positional --emit-only ... must print only the pinned readiness-bypass disclosure', and R6.3(a) round-2 G5 mandates the test verbatim ('a test drives positional --emit-only with --spec and a title-unreferenced ready bead and asserts the preview proceeds with the bypass line, with no exclusion report and no false readiness claim'); R6.1 adds 'a test pins both behaviors'. The implementation prints the line (runEmitOnly positional branch) but `grep -rn 'bead fetched by ID' --include='*_test.go'` finds nothing. The commit message claims 'AC-9/AC-10/AC-10b/AC-15 fixtures'; AC-10's exception leg is the one fixture not delivered.

findings.title: CLI AC-10 test exercises the AC-10b path, not SelectNamedFromReadySet
findings.detail: TestNextSelection_PositionalExcludedByFilter_NamesReason builds an epic with ONE bead (the excluded one), so BuildReadySet returns emptyAfterFilterError before SelectNamedFromReadySet/exclusionReasonForName ever runs — the assertions pass via the AC-10b message, which happens to contain the bead ID and 'excluded'. The genuine positional-exclusion path is covered only at unit level (TestSelectNamedFromReadySet_ExcludedPositionalNamesReason, which I ran green). A sharper CLI fixture: two beads, one kept + one excluded, positional-claim the excluded one. Non-blocking since the observable AC behavior is asserted and the unit leg pins the mechanism.

findings.title: ResolveSpecPrefixProven can emit a false 'no spec found' on a transiently-recovering bd (theoretical)
findings.detail: In target.go, when FindEpicBySpecIDWithCache fails (bd down), epicErr is discarded and flow falls to draftSpecStatusWithCache. The cache does NOT memoize errors, so its AllEpics re-fetches; if bd recovered in the interim on an epic-bearing spec, draftSpecStatus finds the epic, returns (false, nil), and Proven concludes 'no spec found matching' — a false nonexistence claim of exactly the class this spec targets. The common bd-down case IS honest (AllEpics guard errors both times), and the window is a sub-invocation transient flip, so this is advisory. beads.go's scopeResolutionRefusal handles the analogous case better by falling back to epicErr; Proven could do the same: if the initial epicErr is a genuine query failure (not the 'no epic found' sentinel), return it instead of the nonexistence message.
